mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it indicates a weakening labor market that typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate above 5.5% but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and rise in industrial production indicates a strengthening labor market and expanding manufacturing sector, which together drive positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of UNRATE decline and INDPRO rise occurs but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes characterized by high housing starts, the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches peak activity and monetary policy tightening looms, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes (HOUST > 1100 thousand units), S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index signals robust manufacturing activity that typically supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index exceeds 2.5% annualized, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger premature monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL above 2.5% but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer prices and declining retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a weakening consumer sector amid inflation, which typically leads to negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL rise and RSAFS decline occurs but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes of high employment growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), the labor market is so tight that it pressures wage growth and inflation, leading to a Fed tightening cycle that causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In high employment growth regimes (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
